project_type: EaseMyOffice CRM — TanStack Start + React 19 SPA with Supabase (Postgres + RLS + Deno edge functions) backend, hosted on Cloudflare Workers. HRMS (attendance/leave/payroll) is built inside the same app.
language: TypeScript (React 19, TSX); Deno TypeScript for Supabase edge functions; SQL for migrations.
build_system: Bun package manager + Vite build. Scripts in package.json: build=`vite build`, test=`vitest run`. tsc via `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` (npx/node often missing from PATH — prefer the local binary, or export PATH to the nvm node bin as AGENT_CONTEXT.md §4 describes).
test_framework: Vitest unit tests living beside the lib they cover as src/lib/*.test.ts. Pure logic (date math, rules, validation) is unit-tested; no DB/network in tests. A test enforces that src/lib/attendance-rules.ts is byte-identical to supabase/functions/_shared/attendance-rules.ts.
verification_instructions: Full local gate before handoff (AGENT_CONTEXT.md §4): 1) `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (if deps not present). 2) typecheck: `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` (export PATH to node if the binary is missing). 3) `bun run test` (all Vitest files must pass). 4) `bun run build` (regenerates src/routeTree.gen.ts if any route file was added/removed — commit it). Edge functions can optionally be type-checked with `npx -y deno check supabase/functions/<fn>/index.ts` (CI does NOT check them; delete any deno.lock it leaves). There are no Supabase credentials in the sandbox, so SQL cannot be executed and generated types cannot be regenerated here — DB access is only validated by the owner after deploy.
snapshot_or_generated_files: src/routeTree.gen.ts is generated by `bun run build` and must be committed when a route file is added or removed. No other generated/snapshot files are relevant. src/integrations/supabase/types.ts is NOT regenerable in the sandbox (no credentials); new HRMS tables are accessed via the `hrmsDb()` cast helper + hand-written row types in src/lib/hrms.ts rather than through generated types.
setup_instructions: cd /projects/sandbox/Easemyoffice. If node_modules is absent run `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. The npm registry is reachable so the full pipeline runs in-sandbox. Node/npx may be missing from a fresh shell PATH; the local tsc binary at ./node_modules/.bin/tsc is reliable. /tmp is NOT writable — put any scratch files outside the repo under /projects/sandbox/<name> and delete them.
environment_constraints: Network: package registry reachable (full build/test/typecheck runs locally). NO Supabase credentials — cannot run SQL, cannot exercise real data, cannot regenerate types.ts. DB migrations are APPLIED MANUALLY BY THE OWNER (full idempotent SQL pasted in chat): the app must never assume a migration auto-ran. Cannot push or open PRs — the orchestrator publishes locally-committed work. No Docker. Lint: CI does not lint and the repo carries thousands of pre-existing prettier errors, so repo-wide lint fails; new files must be prettier-clean and touched files must gain no new eslint errors.
contribution_requirements: Strictly ADDITIVE and backward-compatible: existing leave, reactive WFH-on-punch (decide_remote), attendance, payroll, idle tracking and the admin command center must keep working unchanged. Permissions enforced SERVER-SIDE only (RLS + edge-function role checks) — never trust the client; employees can read/insert/cancel only their OWN rows and can never self-approve. Point-in-time effects on an `attendance` row must go through the shared pure rules so worked-minutes/status stay consistent. Migrations idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS, DROP POLICY IF EXISTS). The pure-rules file must stay byte-identical between src/lib and supabase/functions/_shared (enforced by a test). User-facing copy says 'admin', never 'HR'.
key_patterns: Request+decision model mirrors leave_requests (migration 20260516000007): a table with employee_id, status pending/approved/rejected/cancelled, decided_by/at, admin_note, created_at + updated_at (trigger hrms_touch_updated_at), RLS = admin OR own-via-employees.profile_id for SELECT, no write policies (edge function is the only writer via service role). Edge function hr-requests (supabase/functions/hr-requests/index.ts) is the pattern for new actions: resolve caller JWT -> employees row for employee actions, gate admin actions on user_roles.role='admin', validate per-type (BACKDATE_DAYS=7 window, overlap/duplicate guards), reply 200 {ok:true|...} or 200 {ok:false,message}, notify via ../_shared/hr-notify.ts (notifyAdmins on create, notifyUser on decision; both best-effort). Browser calls edge functions via hrRequest() in src/lib/attendance-client.ts (throws on {ok:false}). Pure date/rule helpers live in src/lib/attendance-rules.ts (IST via fixed +05:30 offset, addDays, istParts, weekdayOf, closeDay, lateMinutes, windowMinutes, normalizeSchedules). The reactive WFH flow already exists: a login outside the geofence becomes a pending remote request on the attendance row, approved by admin action decide_remote. UI: My Attendance (src/routes/_authenticated/attendance.tsx) uses Card/Dialog/Textarea/Input/Button/Badge/Checkbox from src/components/ui and TanStack Query; admin Approvals (src/routes/_authenticated/hrms/approvals.tsx) lists pending WFH + leave with an approve/reject note row; the /hrms layout (src/routes/_authenticated/hrms.tsx) shows a pending-count badge on the Approvals tab.

directory_structure: src/routes/_authenticated/ holds route components (attendance.tsx = employee My Attendance; hrms.tsx = admin hub layout with glass tabs + guard; hrms/ = admin tabs: attendance, approvals, employees, salary, settings, index). src/lib/ holds shared logic + tests (hrms.ts types, attendance-rules.ts pure rules, attendance-queries.ts read helpers, attendance-client.ts edge-fn wrappers). src/components/hrms/ holds HRMS UI pieces (attendance-month.tsx, glass-tabs, quick-punch, import-team-dialog). supabase/functions/ holds Deno edge functions (hr-requests, attendance-punch) + _shared (attendance-rules.ts byte-identical copy, hr-notify.ts). supabase/migrations/ holds idempotent SQL applied by the owner.
